hypothesis: modbus_reply reads a two-byte address unconditionally without first verifying that req_length reaches offset+3. A short or addressless Modbus/TCP request, including Report Slave ID, Read Exception Status, or an unknown function, may contain only the backend header and function byte, causing reads beyond a tightly sized request object.
evidence_source: At lines 721-724 the function uses `req[offset + 1]` and `req[offset + 2]` before dispatching on the function and without any req_length check. Meanwhile compute_meta_length_after_function returns zero for addressless and unknown indication functions at lines 267-269, so _modbus_receive_msg can complete such a TCP request without receiving address bytes.

expected_behavior: If the received request is stored in an object sized to the returned req_length, calling modbus_reply causes an AddressSanitizer heap- or stack-buffer-overflow report for the reads at line 724; with an oversized caller buffer it instead reads bytes outside the received message and uses indeterminate/stale data.

notes: Common callers may allocate a maximum-ADU buffer, masking the physical over-read, but modbus_reply receives req_length and does not enforce a minimum before accessing the request. For RTU, checksum bytes may also mask the access; Modbus/TCP has no trailing checksum.
